identity.name: Leaf Lens
identity.value_proposition: Spot common houseplant diseases from a single leaf photo.
identity.target_users: Hobby gardeners who want a quick second opinion before treating a plant.

requirements.text: A user can classify a leaf photo into a known disease or healthy.
requirements.acceptance: Given a labelled validation set, when the model classifies it, then top-1 accuracy is at least 85%.

components.name: ml
components.responsibility: Trains and evaluates the leaf classifier.

releases.process: Tag a calendar version on main when a model is promoted.

ml.seeds: fixed seeds recorded in the run config

decisions.title: Product identity
decisions.context: The project needed a name, audience and a measurable requirement before any code.
decisions.decision: Leaf Lens targets hobby gardeners, with one accuracy-tested requirement.
decisions.consequences: Features outside R1 need a new requirement first.

decisions.title: One Python ML package
decisions.context: The product is a model plus its evaluation; there is no UI yet.
decisions.decision: A single Python component at the repository root.
decisions.consequences: A UI later means switching to a monorepo layout.

decisions.title: One package, no contracts
decisions.context: A single component calls nothing else.
decisions.decision: ml trains and evaluates the model.
decisions.consequences: A served model later needs a contract.

decisions.title: Typed exceptions
decisions.context: The package is used from code and notebooks.
decisions.decision: ml raises typed exceptions whose messages say how to fix the input.

decisions.title: Unit and integration tests
decisions.consequences: Integration tests run on a small fixture dataset.

decisions.title: No UI
decisions.context: The project has no user interface.
decisions.decision: There is no visual system to define.

decisions.title: README is the user documentation
decisions.context: A single model package used by its maintainer and a few gardeners.
decisions.decision: External docs live in the README; no paths are mapped yet.
decisions.consequences: Map paths in docs/principles.toml once the package has a public interface.

decisions.title: CI on GitHub Actions, packaged, not deployed
decisions.context: The model runs on developer machines only.
decisions.decision: GitHub Actions runs the checks; the component builds as a package.
decisions.consequences: No environments or hosting until the model is served.

decisions.title: No secrets, no auth
decisions.context: The model runs on developer machines.
decisions.decision: Nothing is deployed, so there is no secret store and no auth.
decisions.consequences: Revisit when the model is served.

decisions.title: Monthly Dependabot updates
decisions.context: ML libraries move fast but break often.
decisions.decision: Dependabot opens monthly update pull requests.

decisions.title: Observability not applicable yet
decisions.decision: No logging setup until the model is served.

decisions.title: Calendar versions per promoted model
decisions.context: Releases are model promotions, not API changes.
decisions.decision: A calver tag on main marks each promoted model.
decisions.consequences: The tag names the code and data that produced the model.

decisions.title: DVC data, fixed seeds, MLflow runs
decisions.decision: Datasets are versioned with DVC, seeds are fixed in the run config, runs are tracked in MLflow.
decisions.consequences: Any result can be traced to its data, seed and code.

decisions.title: No accessibility target
decisions.context: The project has no user interface.

decisions.title: No performance budgets
decisions.context: Training time varies with the data.

decisions.title: Conventional commits on trunk
decisions.context: A solo maintainer with agents committing needs a predictable history.
decisions.decision: Conventional commits scoped by component, committed straight to trunk.
decisions.consequences: The commit-msg hook rejects messages that break the convention.

decisions.title: Review every task
decisions.context: Model and data changes are easy to get subtly wrong.
decisions.decision: Review after every task, and treat data/ as a risk path.
decisions.consequences: Slower iteration in exchange for earlier review.
